text:
Evan Rodrigues won two Stanley Cups in Florida and moved to New Jersey this season, and his best night as a Devil came Nov. 14: two goals and an assist in a 7-4 win over Washington. He has 6 goals and 11 points in 22 games on about 15 and a half minutes a night.

The goals are running a little hot, about two ahead of his chances. The bigger concern is five on five: New Jersey's expected goal share (the quality of chances) is about seven points worse with him on the ice than without him, the kind of gap that eventually costs a veteran middle-six spot. Some of that is bad on-ice luck pulling his results down, but not all of it.

Last season in Florida, Evolving-Hockey had him worth 0.9 wins, mostly from defense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a clean breakout game (64% of his exits keep possession) and a lot of shots, though fewer from the slot than his volume suggests. Watch whether he gets inside. When he shoots from the perimeter, his line drifts.
